rule: Every individual stock belongs to exactly one group. Funds deliberately overlap the stocks they hold, and that hidden overlap is the lesson the game teaches, so the one-group rule applies to stocks only.
note: The AI group is defined by basket.json, which is frozen at the prereg tag. basket.json is authoritative: the symbols repeated here are for readability and a test checks the two files still agree.
history_note: full_history means the ticker has daily prices for the whole 10-year window that starts in December 2016. Only VRT and PLTR, both in the AI group, are false.

tickers.reason: The largest consumer tech company, but it sells devices rather than AI computing.
Salesforce sells business software subscriptions; AI is a feature, not the main engine.
Adobe sells creative software, and AI image tools are arguably a threat to it.
Most of Cisco's sales still come from networking for ordinary businesses, though its AI orders are growing.
Intel makes chips but largely missed the AI boom, so it tests whether 'chipmaker' alone means 'AI bet'.
The largest US bank, and the non-AI stock representing banks in Hypothesis 1.
A second large US bank, so players can see two banks move almost as one.
An investment bank, which earns differently from the two lenders above.
The largest US oil company; its price follows oil, not technology.
A second oil major, for the same 'two of a kind' lesson as the banks.
A driller with no refining, so it tracks the oil price more directly.
A large, steady drugmaker, and the non-AI stock representing health care in Hypothesis 1.
A health insurer, which earns from premiums rather than from drugs.
A drugmaker dependent on a few patents, so it moves on its own news.
Household basics people buy in any economy, and the non-AI stock representing consumer staples in Hypothesis 1.
Drinks sold worldwide, with demand that barely changes year to year.
The largest US retailer, which tends to hold up when shoppers trade down.
All non-US stocks in one fund; one of the 6 preset funds.
Developed markets only (Europe, Japan), which move closely with the US.
Emerging markets, the holding least tied to the US market.
The whole US bond market; the preset that adds little risk, which is the point.
Gold, which often moves independently of shares.
Long-term government bonds, which swing on interest rates.
Company bonds, which fall with shares in a crash, unlike government bonds.
The S&P 500 in one fund, for the '500 names, far fewer bets' lesson.
The whole US market; the broad fund required by Hypothesis 1's beginner set.
The Nasdaq-100 tech fund, required by level 4's 30% rule.

benchmarks.reason: The S&P 500 index, used to define market stress days as the worst 10% of its daily returns, and reported beside RSP in Hypothesis 2.
The equal-weight S&P 500, the benchmark for Hypothesis 2's verdict, where each AI stock is about 0.2% of the index.
